title: When the ice came south: the ice ages mapped, and what lies under them today
excerpt: I mapped the Northern Hemisphere's ice sheets at 18 moments of the last 3.6 million years. The last ice age was only the 4th largest; 709 of today's cities and towns, New York among them, stand on ground its ice covered.
seo_description: The Northern Hemisphere's ice sheets in 18 time slices: their size, how far south they reached, the cities beneath them and the land the sea gave up.
header_alt: Title card reading 'When the ice came south' in black and glacier blue on pale paper, beside a map of the Arctic seen from above the pole with white ice sheets over North America and northern Eurasia at their largest, in MIS 6, a red dashed line for the smaller ice of the Last Glacial Maximum, and sand-coloured shelves where the sea floor would be dry. Text: at their largest, in MIS 6, 33.8 million km².
